title: Peter Carlsson Hands Over Northvolt With One Week of Cash Left
conflicts: Headcount: about 6,600 staff (Reuters, Nov 2024) vs over 5,000 (Northvolt release, Mar 2025), close to 5,000 (Johnstone via The Local) and about 5,000 (AFP/Fortune); story uses about 5,000 for March 2025 only. Money raised: more than $10bn in equity, debt and public financing (Reuters) vs owners' capital ~90bn kronor plus ~60bn kronor debt (The Local); Reuters phrasing used. Debts $5.8bn (Reuters, Fortune) vs $5.84bn (The Local); $5.8bn used. September 2024 cuts: 1,600 announced, slightly over 1,300 after negotiations (The Local); story says 1,600 announced. Founding 2016 (Reuters, CNBC, Fortune) vs 2015 (The Local); 2016 used.
notes: Episode centred on Carlsson stepping down on 22 Nov 2024, the day after the US Chapter 11 filing, with the March 2025 Swedish bankruptcy (filed under interim leadership) and Lyten's February 2026 purchase as aftermath. Funding changed from venture to mixed (equity, debt and public financing per Reuters). Blame limited to Carlsson's own words ('over-ambitious on the timing') and the company's stated reasons; unnamed-source explanations and the share-sale controversy not used. Quote stance: complicates.
